hints: Focus on the phrase every pair of adjacent elements, it means the trend must work with no exceptions from Na to Cl.
Think about nuclear charge across Period 3, protons increase while shielding stays similar, so what happens to atomic size every step?
Recall the two famous dips in 1st ionisation energy and the rise then fall in melting point, and check if either can be a smooth decrease.
walkthrough:
**Understand what every pair means**

Great question to slow down for. It is not asking for the overall change from Na to Cl. It is asking if the value falls for Na to Mg, AND Mg to Al, AND Al to Si, and so on, with no rises in between.

**Check statement 1, atomic radius**

Across Period 3, proton number increases but electrons go into the same shell, so shielding hardly changes. The greater nuclear attraction pulls the outer shell in closer each time.

Trend rule:
$$ \text{increasing proton number + similar shielding} \rightarrow \text{smaller atomic radius} $$
This happens for every adjacent pair from Na to Cl, so statement 1 is true.

**Check statement 2, 1st ionisation energy**

Generally 1st ionisation energy increases across a period because the smaller, more highly charged atoms hold electrons tighter. But Period 3 has two well known exceptions.

$$ \text{Mg} > \text{Al and P} > \text{S} $$
Al is lower than Mg due to the $3p$ vs $3s$ subshell, and S is lower than P due to spin-pair repulsion. Because it goes up then down, it does not decrease between every pair, so statement 2 is false.

**Check statement 3, melting point**

Think about structure. Melting point rises from Na to Si as metallic bonding gets stronger then giant covalent bonding in Si gives a very high value. Then it drops sharply for P, S, Cl which are simple molecular.

$$ \text{Na < Mg < Al < Si (peak) > P > S > Cl} $$
Because it first increases then decreases, it does not decrease between every pair, so statement 3 is false.

**Conclude the answer**

Only statement 1 is true for every adjacent pair. That combination matches option D.

options.A: Incorrect. This would mean all three statements are true. Statements 2 and 3 both have exceptions, so this cannot be right.
options.B: Incorrect. This would mean statements 1 and 2 are true. Statement 1 is true, but statement 2 fails because 1st ionisation energy generally increases with dips at Al and S, it does not fall every step.
options.C: Incorrect. This would mean statements 1 and 3 are true, or 2 and 3 depending on paper code. Statement 3 fails because melting point rises to silicon then falls, it does not fall between every pair.
options.D: Correct. Only statement 1 is true. Atomic radius falls for every adjacent pair due to increasing nuclear charge with similar shielding, while ionisation energy and melting point both show rises and falls.
